issues.body: For an unknown `if`, `_taint_block()` unions the ending taint sets of both arms, and `_record_printed_keys()` credits the post-join print if either arm leaves `repos` tainted. For example, a resolver with `if requested: repos = enabled` and `else: repos = ["some-owner/some-name"]` still reports `["repos"]`: the manual arm donates policy taint while the scheduled arm silently sweeps a hand-copied subset. The newly added one-branch positive test requires precisely this existential join and does not prove the separate membership-validation control that the comments rely on. The overwrite/dead-code mutants only make the published name untainted on all live arms, so they do not exercise this prior-round bypass.
issues.fix_hint: Make the analysis prove authorization/completeness on every executable path reaching the output, while explicitly recognizing the shipped manual path's `requested in enabled` validation rather than treating any one tainted arm as sufficient. Add a named non-crashing mutant of the live resolver whose scheduled arm publishes a copied subset while another live arm remains policy-derived; it must make `resolve_policy_derived_outputs` empty and preserve the pristine self-test row count.
issues.title: Union joins still certify a hardcoded live branch

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-4 major remains. The new ordered strong updates catch a hardcode that replaces the value on both incoming paths, but the unknown-branch join is still existential: one policy-derived arm taints the name after the join even when another live arm publishes a copied list. The new positive branch test deliberately pins that union behavior and still does not model or prove the manual arm's membership check. Thus `resolve_policy_derived_outputs` can remain `["repos"]` while the scheduled arm is a hardcoded subset, provided the other arm assigns a policy-derived value; the scheduled sweep-completeness claim is then green after being severed. No cross-branch hardcode mutant was added. This is materially the same soundness gap at the same severity, so progress is stagnant.
